title.narrative: Emergency Relief and Recovery for IDPs, Returnees and Vulnerable Communities in Yei South Sudan

description.narrative:
The armed conflict has caused influx of people from the rural areas and from other counties into Yei River County and other county headquarters in the Catholic Diocese of Yei. The increased number of people has generated increased demand for food and other basic services as water, medicines and shelter. In the three counties in Western Equatoria State, conflict between native farmers and encroaching cattle keepers exploded, which – displaced 367 households, and destroyed property and farms. Furthermore, deterioration of security situation in Mundri Town, Lui, Wonduruba in Lainya County and in Kajo-Keji County resulted in additional displacement of over 10,500 people. IDPs are unable to return to their home villages without any form of support such as shelter materials to rebuild their houses or tools for cultivation. Needs identified for affected communities are: shelter and non-food items for 3000 households and seeds and tools for 3000 households.
Reports coming from Yei diocese recently indicated that number of households are retuning back to their home of origin Wonduruba, with some number of IDPs remaining in the diocese from nearby Counties of Mundri and Maridi.
